summary: The lecture traces the constitutional development of India from the Regulating Act 1773 to the Indian Independence Act 1947. It covers key legislations like Pitt's India Act, Charter Acts, Government of India Acts, and Indian Councils Acts, highlighting centralization, dyarchy, separate electorates, and provincial autonomy. The evolution from Company rule to Crown rule, introduction of civil services, legislative reforms, and the 1935 Act's federal structure are emphasized. Finally, the August Offer, Cripps Mission, and the 1947 Act leading to independence and partition are discussed.
points: Regulating Act 1773 established Supreme Court at Calcutta and created Governor-General of Bengal.
Pitt's India Act 1784 created Board of Control for political affairs and Court of Directors for commercial affairs.
Charter Act 1813 ended EIC trade monopoly except tea and China trade; allocated ₹1 lakh annually for education.
Charter Act 1833 made Governor-General of Bengal as Governor-General of India; EIC became purely administrative body.
Charter Act 1853 separated legislative and executive functions; introduced open competition for civil services.
Government of India Act 1858 transferred power from Company to Crown; created Secretary of State for India with 15-member council; Viceroy appointed.
Indian Councils Act 1861 introduced portfolio system; associated Indians (Raja of Benares, Maharaja of Patiala, Sir Dinkar Rao) with law-making.
Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto) introduced separate electorates for Muslims; first Indian (Satyendra Prasad Sinha) in Viceroy's Executive Council.
Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy in provinces (Reserved/Transferred subjects); bicameral central legislature; Central Public Service Commission.
Government of India Act 1935 proposed All-India Federation with three lists (Federal, Provincial, Concurrent); provincial autonomy; Federal Court; RBI established.

check.q: Which Act ended the East India Company's trade monopoly in India except for tea and trade with China?
The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy in provinces, dividing subjects into Reserved and Transferred lists. Which of the following was a feature of the Reserved subjects?
opts: Administered by Governor with Executive Council, not accountable to legislature
Administered by ministers responsible to legislature

check.q: The Government of India Act 1935 proposed an All-India Federation comprising British India and Princely States. Which of the following was NOT a feature of this Act?
opts: Three-fold division of legislative subjects (Federal, Provincial, Concurrent)
Dyarchy abolished at provincial level and introduced at centre (though never implemented)
